senses.gloss:
aṭavī (CII 1), the forest-folk. RE XIII of Aśoka seems to speak of the Aṭavī or foresters as habitually criminal.
 (SITI), troops.

āṭavika (Ep. Ind., Vol. XIV, p. 303, text line 50), a kind of grains.
 (EI 20; HD), an officer in charge of forest tracts. See Arthaśāstra, I 12 (mentioned among the 18 tīrthas).
Aṭṭapati (HD), the market-master. Cf. Rājataraṅgiṇī, V. 167.
aṭṭapati-bhāga (HRS), office entrusted with the collection of the share of the lord of the market, as indicated by the Rājataraṅgiṇī; literally, ‘share of the market-master’.
aṭṭaṇaikkāl (SITI), Tamil; a kind of stand or pedestal (probably of eight legs).
